title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 1st District
area: Eastern North Carolina, including Elizabeth City, Rocky Mount and Goldsboro.

context.text: North Carolina redrew its congressional district boundaries in October 2025, and District 1 is now rated R+5 on the Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index under the new lines. Incumbent Donald Davis (D) is seeking re-election against Laurie Buckhout (R) and Tom Bailey (L).

candidates.name: Donald Davis

summary.text: Don Davis is the Democratic incumbent seeking a third term in North Carolina's 1st Congressional District, now redrawn to lean more Republican. A Snow Hill native, Air Force Academy graduate and Air Force veteran, he was an Air Force ROTC instructor at East Carolina University, mayor of Snow Hill and a North Carolina state senator before his election to Congress in 2022. He is ranking member of the Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development.

background.text: Born and raised in Snow Hill, North Carolina, where he worked in tobacco fields as a young man and, according to his official biography, attends and ministers at the church he attended growing up.

Graduated from the U.S. Air Force Academy in 1994 with a bachelor's degree in social sciences, and later earned a master's degree in administration from Central Michigan University, a master's in sociology with a concentration in regional development, and a doctorate in education from East Carolina University.

Served eight years on active duty as an Air Force officer; as a first lieutenant he coordinated Air Force One and congressional delegation (CODEL) operations at Andrews Air Force Base and supported military families as a mortuary officer.

Returned to eastern North Carolina as an assistant professor of Aerospace Studies with East Carolina University's Air Force ROTC Detachment 600, teaching national security affairs, military history and leadership; describes more than 20 years as an educator.
Became the youngest mayor of Snow Hill at age 29 and served seven years.
Was elected to the North Carolina State Senate in 2008 and served 12 years, according to his official biography.
Won the 1st District seat in 2022 after Rep. G. K. Butterfield's retirement and was re-elected in 2024 by a 5,826-vote margin over Laurie Buckhout, who is his opponent again in 2026.

Serves on the House Agriculture Committee (ranking member of the Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, appointed in 2025) and the House Armed Services Committee (vice ranking member), and co-chairs the For Country Caucus.
Lives in Greene County with his wife, Yuvonka; they have three sons, Ryan, Justin and Kyler.

priorities.text: Congressman Davis' top priority in Congress is expanding access to affordable health care because he knows it is vital to keeping rural hospitals open, making health care accessible to those who need it most, and improving treatment for victims of addiction.

As the Vice Ranking Member of the House Committee on Agriculture, Congressman Davis is fighting for fair and just policies and investments that promote equity and accommodate the diversity of the district's agricultural products.

positions.summary: Cosponsor of the COVER Now Act to help states expand Medicaid, and relaunched the State Medicaid Expansion Caucus to close the Medicaid coverage gap.
Led legislation, the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, to end tax breaks that data center and Big Tech companies received under the 2025 reconciliation law.
positions.quote: Washington is giving handouts to Big Tech companies while American families are drowning

record.text: Serves as ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, and as vice ranking member of the House Armed Services Committee, also sitting on its Readiness and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees.
Introduced H.R. 10448, the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, to exclude data centers from bonus depreciation and Opportunity Zone tax breaks created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

candidates.name: Laurie Buckhout

summary.text: Laurie Buckhout is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Donald Davis in North Carolina's redrawn 1st Congressional District, a rematch of the 2024 general election, which Davis won. She is a retired U.S. Army colonel who founded and later sold a cyber and electronic warfare consulting business and served in the Pentagon's cyber policy office. Her campaign describes her as a "constitutional conservative" running on lowering costs, securing the border and strengthening national defense.

background.text: Born in Virginia and lives in Edenton, North Carolina, with her husband Paul, a retired Army officer; they have two sons, according to her campaign website.

Earned a bachelor's degree from James Madison University, a master's of military arts and science in national military strategy, and a master's of science in information management from Webster University.

Was commissioned a second lieutenant in the Army Signal Corps in 1984 and served 26 years, retiring as a colonel in 2010; according to a candidate-supplied biography, she commanded a task force in the initial attack into Iraq in 2003.
After retiring from the Army, founded Corvus Consulting, which specialized in electronic warfare and cyberspace operations; it was sold to Castellum Inc. in 2019, according to SIGNAL Media.
Served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy and was later named acting Assistant Secretary of War for cyber policy by President Trump.
Was the Republican nominee in 2024 and lost the general election to Davis.
Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary over Carteret County Sheriff Asa Buck, 23,531 votes to 20,974.

priorities.text: Lowering costs and cutting taxes for families in Eastern North Carolina.
Border security, including resourcing border patrol agents.
Cutting regulations affecting farmers and fishermen, and supporting the military and veterans.

positions.summary: Says she will stand strong against what she describes as additional red tape on law-abiding gun owners, citing her background as a combat veteran.
positions.quote: She will stand strong against the extremists who mock our hunting heritage and would punish law-abiding gun owners with additional red tape.

positions.summary: Asked about the Supreme Court ruling against the administration's tariffs, said President Trump should have the authority and that the tariffs put the U.S. on an equal footing on trade.
positions.quote: We've been taken advantage of for decades with unfair trade practices, and this is putting America back on an equal footing.

candidates.researchNotes: Buckhout has not held elected office, so there is no voting or bill-sponsorship record. Positions are from her campaign website issues page and a February 2026 interview reported by The Assembly. No statements found on rent regulation, school choice, minimum wage, or voter citizenship proof.

statements.quote: Border security is national security. Laurie will focus on ensuring our border patrol agents have the resources they need to keep dangerous drugs out of our country.

candidates.name: Tom Bailey
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Tom Bailey is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 1st Congressional District. He is a Vietnam veteran and longtime Libertarian activist who has worked on ballot access and election law. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he lists protecting individual liberty, election integrity and limiting taxation among his priorities.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 1968 to 1971; earned a high school diploma from South Bakersfield High School and graduated from the University of North Carolina, Wilmington in 1993.
Says he has managed and supported numerous local and state campaigns and has spent decades supporting ballot access and constitutional governance in North Carolina.
Served on the Libertarian Party of North Carolina Executive Committee and as chairman of its Legal Action Committee, where he helped lead the federal ballot-access lawsuit McLoughlin v. Marsh.
Ran as a Libertarian for U.S. House in North Carolina's 13th District in 2018 and in the 1st District in 2024, losing both general elections; this is his third congressional run.

priorities.text: Restoring voting rights of citizens to put control of government back in the hands of the people.
Major federal tax reform limiting the federal government to taxing only state governments.
Restoring the Bill of Rights with an emphasis on due process.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Bailey's 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website was located and the survey lists no stance on the guide's listed issues; no news coverage quoting him on them was found.
